claims.text: Microsoft documents token-based document access filtering against synchronized permission metadata in Azure AI Search; native features are preview.
claims.source_title: Document-level access control in Azure AI Search
claims.research_note: The documented API is 2026-08-01-preview. This establishes supported behavior, not independent verification of a customer deployment.

claims.text: Microsoft documents that SharePoint parent-scope permission changes require explicit refresh, while supported unique item ACL changes can be picked up incrementally in recent previews.
claims.research_note: Limitations and synchronization sections distinguish inheritance changes from item ACL changes. Undated page accessed at cutoff.

claims.text: Microsoft recommends its remote SharePoint knowledge source for the full SharePoint permission model; it calls the Copilot retrieval API with governance in SharePoint.
claims.research_note: Important box describes an alternative architecture; no claim about universal downstream cache deletion.

claims.text: Microsoft describes an enterprise project that materialized SharePoint permissions into downstream search and retrieval and planned periodic re-ingestion.
claims.source_title: Propagating SharePoint Document Permissions to AI Systems
claims.research_note: Primary engineering case narrative, unnamed customer; no customer incidence rate or Concord buying evidence.

claims.text: Glean documents permission mirroring and signed-in identity checks across search, AI answers, agents, MCP and embedded surfaces, plus exportable administration audit records.
claims.research_note: Product documentation supports current workflow. Universal no-leak language is not independently established.

claims.text: Glean publicly documents SaaS and customer-hosted deployment models and security/architecture guidance.
claims.research_note: Customer-hosted deployment is therefore not unique to Concord.

claims.text: Airbyte announced Airbyte Agents on May 4, 2026, describing a Context Store, live connectors, Python SDK and MCP access.
claims.source_title: Airbyte Agents: A New Era for Airbyte
claims.research_note: Vendor launch describes active expansion from replication toward agent context; performance claims not reused.

claims.text: Airbyte markets permission-aware context, query-time authorization and logged agent data access.
claims.source_title: What Is AI Agent Security and How Does It Work?
claims.research_note: Marketing explanation, not an independently exercised authorization test or universal integration guarantee.

claims.text: Unstructured documents partitioning, extraction, enrichment, chunking and embedding, with source-to-vector-database pipelines.
claims.research_note: Ingestion capability is documented; this claim makes no assertion of closed-loop identity verification.

claims.text: Oso publishes a Python/Postgres/pgvector RAG authorization example using local authorization to reduce application-data synchronization requirements.
claims.source_title: The Right Approach to Authorization in RAG
claims.research_note: Reference implementation is evidence that authorized RAG is an existing build pattern, not proof of production coverage at arbitrary customers.

claims.text: AuthZed documents permission filtering for Pinecone retrieval using SpiceDB relationship checks, including pre-filter and post-filter approaches.
claims.source_title: Access Control in RAG with Pinecone and SpiceDB
claims.research_note: Documentation includes executable integration patterns and explains tradeoffs.

claims.text: AuthZed published an agentic RAG example with authorization embedded in a LangGraph pipeline.
claims.source_title: Build a production-grade Agentic RAG system using AuthZed Cloud
claims.research_note: LangGraph plus authorization is already publicly documented and cannot be claimed as a moat.

claims.text: LangSmith documents offline dataset evaluations and online production evaluations, including code evaluators, traces and feedback loops.
claims.research_note: Evaluation substrate could support an in-house substitute; no implication that it is a cross-source remediation product.

claims.text: LangSmith documents controls for preventing sensitive inputs and outputs from being sent in traces.
claims.source_title: Prevent logging of sensitive data in traces
claims.research_note: Relevant to optional observability integration and customer-runtime boundary.

claims.text: Onyx documents source ACL synchronization for selected Enterprise Edition connectors and separately configurable refresh and pruning.
claims.source_title: Managing connectors and data sources in Onyx
claims.research_note: Overview lists supported permission-sync sources and connector lifecycle. Do not assume all sources or all deployments have the same settings.

claims.text: Onyx documents local self-hosting, cloud availability, agents and internal search.
claims.research_note: Cloud and self-hostable product are documented; specific enterprise entitlements require separate commercial verification.

claims.text: Paragon documents incremental syncs, periodic full syncs and deletion events for records deleted or unshared from the connecting account.
claims.research_note: Default full refresh is documented as 24 hours; this is not necessarily per-user permission refresh latency.

claims.text: Paragon documents permission synchronization into a fine-grained authorization server, with query-time pre/post/hybrid filtering for supported file integrations.
claims.research_note: Technical docs use a synchronized permission model; do not call it a guaranteed upstream live check.

claims.text: Nango documents explicit deletion handling for incremental syncs and automatic missing-record detection for full syncs.
claims.research_note: Provides useful connector primitives without proving final downstream user retrieval behavior.

claims.text: Ragie describes embedded RAG connectors with authentication, permissions, automatic syncing and connection lifecycle webhooks.
claims.research_note: Official launch verified; docs home returned HTTP 502, so exact source-ACL semantics were not established.

claims.text: Letta documents deleting a memory block removes it from all agents with that block attached.
claims.research_note: Specific block semantics only; no claim that source-derived copies or conversation history are universally removed.

claims.text: The SciPhi-AI/R2R repository describes an agentic retrieval system exposed through a REST API.
claims.research_note: Repository establishes project existence and declared interface; no enterprise-readiness or exact permission-propagation claim.

claims.text: LangGraph documents durable orchestration for long-running stateful agents and can be used without LangChain.
claims.research_note: Framework role, not a Concord production-readiness claim.

claims.text: LangChain provides agent abstractions, tools and model integrations; its agents build on LangGraph.
claims.research_note: The frameworks are complementary, not interchangeable product builders.

claims.text: No publicly documented support for the complete independently operated Concord workflow was found in this bounded source set as of 2026-09-05.
claims.research_note: This is a scoped finding, not proof of market white space or competitor absence; private features, different terminology and unreviewed products may cover it.

search_scope.location: Current Glean security, Azure AI Search ACL, Paragon sync/permissions, Oso/AuthZed RAG, LangSmith evaluation, Onyx connector and Unstructured core documentation
search_scope.result: Documented adjacent controls. No reviewed source establishes the entire independent cross-vendor source-change to derivative-repair to affected-identity evidence workflow.

claims.text: Concord's incident frequency, reachable paying buyer, budget, paid adoption, retention and expansion are unverified in this research.
claims.research_note: No customer interviews, customer production access, commercial records or paid pilot results were available in the task materials.

search_scope.location: User-provided project context and this public-source strategic opportunity study
search_scope.result: Product vision and technical hypotheses available; verified purchasing and production outcome evidence unavailable.

claims.text: Authorized Crunchbase database/API access was unavailable in this session.
claims.research_note: No Crunchbase connector/API tool was available; no authenticated database queries or subscription export was performed. Public primary-source fallback was used.

search_scope.location: Available tool metadata filtered for Crunchbase
search_scope.result: No specialized authorized Crunchbase capability found.

claims.text: A measurable cross-destination revocation/deletion assurance wedge is worth testing for teams operating custom or mixed AI stacks, but secure RAG alone is insufficient differentiation.
claims.research_note: Existing authorization, ingestion and evaluation features narrow the unproven opportunity to cross-system operational proof.

claims.text: Illustrative annual contract tests use USD 15000, 30000 and 60000, with 1, 3 and 6 paid accounts by month 18. None is a quoted price, pipeline fact or forecast.
claims.research_note: Numbers are selected to test whether a narrow enterprise control can support implementation effort; customers must validate value and willingness to pay.

claims.text: Market sensitivity examples use hypothetical target pools of 2500/10000/25000 organizations, relevant AI shares 20%/35%/50%, severe-pain shares 10%/20%/35% and serviceability 20%/30%/40%.
claims.research_note: These are deliberately unvalidated model inputs, not measured population or adoption estimates; no investment-deck TAM claim should use them.

claims.text: Assumption-only TAM sensitivity outputs are USD 0.75m / 21m / 262.5m; they are model arithmetic, not researched market estimates.
claims.research_note: Wide variation demonstrates missing evidence, especially target account counts, purchase-worthy pain and ACV.
claims.formula: Target organizations × relevant AI share × severe-pain share × assumed annual contract value

claims.text: Pilot targets are three design partners, under two engineer-days integration by the third installation, 1000 probe cases with zero restricted retrieval after containment, and three paid accounts by month 18.
claims.research_note: These are proposed acceptance thresholds and future goals, not achieved results. Probe coverage must be disclosed and does not establish universal safety.
